title: Abdominal Pain

rationale.Non-contrast CT abdomen/pelvis: Gold standard for stone diagnosis. Shows size, location, hydronephrosis.
rationale.Analgesia (Ketorolac / Morphine): Pain management. Ketorolac very effective for renal colic.
rationale.Tamsulosin (medical expulsive therapy): For distal ureteral stones <10mm. Relaxes ureteral smooth muscle.
rationale.Strain urine / Stone analysis: Capture stone for analysis. Metabolic workup if recurrent.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute severe unilateral flank pain radiating to the groin, associated with nausea, vomiting, and hematuria. Pain is colicky — comes in waves as the stone passes. Non-contrast CT abdomen/pelvis is the gold standard for diagnosis. Ultrasound can be used in pregnancy/children. UA shows microscopic or gross hematuria. Most stones are calcium oxalate. Treatment depends on size and location: <5-10mm stones at UVJ or distal ureter → medical expulsive therapy (tamsulosin) + analgesia + IV fluids. Larger stones or proximal location → urology consult for lithotripsy or ureteroscopy. Strain urine and send stone for analysis. Metabolic workup if recurrent. Prevention: increase fluid intake (>2L/day), dietary modifications based on stone type.
